title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s White Day Part 4
text: Now that I’ve arrived in Zeltoble, I’ve finished my final checks and am just waiting for the doors to open. From here on out, it’s all up to the villagers to give it their all.

I’ve taken a quick look at the musicals on the program. One is *The Legend of the Shield Hero*, Act II. Since Filo happens to appear in it, they’ve apparently turned it into a much bigger-scale musical.

I wonder how it’ll turn out with the actual Filo playing the role herself? The second one was *Legends of the Past*, I think? *The Hero of the Staff*… apparently it’s about Trash’s life story. I hear Keel is playing the lead in this one, too.

And for some reason, Trash is appearing in this one as well. I was wondering what role he’d play, but apparently he’s doing an adapted version of the Pig King from Faubrey. Is playing nothing but villains a form of self-deprecation? It feels like he’s approaching his characterization from that angle.

Meanwhile, I’ll check on the condition of the folks competing in the Filolial Race, then head straight back to the venue to check on the attendees. There’s a huge crowd here. Sales of Keel’s merchandise are looking like they might catch up to Filo’s. At this rate, it might only be a matter of time before Keel stops cross-dressing.
“The Keel-kun plushies are sold out!”
Voices of discontent echo from the venue. Did they really sell out even though the price was set pretty high? Or rather, I feel like it hasn’t even been 30 minutes since sales started…
“Waaah. I want a Keel-kun!”

It’s the child from the parent-child pair I saw last time who’s crying. What an incredible line. It sounds just like Keel is being sold as a pet. If you want one that badly, I think you’ll find similar ones for sale at the slave trader’s place.
“What can I do? They’re sold out.”
“I want it! I want it! I want it!”
Um…
“Imiya.”
“Yes! What is it?”
I call out to Imiya, who’s busy working the sales counter. Raphtalia is also swamped, frantically selling Filo merchandise and White Day items.
“For now, make a list of people who’d be okay with pre-ordering the Keel plushies, and let them know we’ll restock them later.”
“O-okay!”

Selling out after preparing three thousand of them—just how popular is Keel as a pet? That loincloth-wearing dog! He used to innocently play around with all sorts of people while peddling his wares. Unlike someone like Filo, he’s approachable, which is why he became so popular.

A bird that pulls a carriage and a friendly dog becoming popular… Are times really changing? By this world’s standards, Keel is a Demi-Human and a Beastman, right? The customers aren’t just from Melromarc, but their sensibilities are different… right? Maybe I’ll set aside some space to sell them while I’m peddling—they seem like they’d sell well long-term.
It looks like we can expect a long-running bestseller, too. Like that bear doll. In my world, it might work as a long-running anime—the kind where kids would say, “This is the one!”

Anyway, once we’d sold off most of the merchandise, the show began. Tickets sold like hotcakes, and the White Day merchandise was returned to Filo and Keel right on the spot. We really just collected the money.
I’ll have to be very careful about karma… I mean, we have to make sure the customers go home satisfied.
“Rafu!”
I wonder why Raph-chan has been playing the role of Raphtalia all this time? If Filo’s playing herself, I feel like Raphtalia would work too… but I have a feeling she’d hate that.

I watch the performance, finding Raph-chan’s acting quite endearing. She sings in various scenes… Filo doesn’t show up at the very beginning. Just as I was thinking that, the background suddenly shifts to what looks like the inside of a slave trader’s tent, and Filo emerges dancing from an egg-shaped object. It’s a bit different from what actually happened, but for the sake of pacing, Filo appears at the exact moment the egg is purchased…
Oh, in some parts, an overexcited Keel turns into a dog. It looks like we’ll even see the Dragon Zombie this time, given the nature of the performance.
“Cure!”
Huh!? Gaelion is playing the Dragon Zombie. I quietly look away. Keel really has a bad habit of turning into a dog whenever he gets excited.

In the scene where he uses the Lars Shield, he’s still acting all cool as a dog. The Filo fans seem completely satisfied with Filo singing and dancing in the background. And so, they somehow managed to defeat the Dragon Zombie. That’s where the curtain falls.
After that, they start performing “Trash’s Half-Life.” The role of the younger sister is… why is Atla even here? Fohl has also snuck in for a cameo role before I knew it.
Wasn’t he supposed to be away on a training journey? Did he just ditch it to join the performance?
“‘Big Brother… Is your work in Melromarc going well?’”
“‘I’m fine…’ Woof woof.”

Oh man… I’m laughing. There’s such a disconnect between the character in the play and Keel’s lines and actions that it’s turned into a comedy. Trash is here, but as he looks at Atla playing the semi-transparent younger sister, he has this distant look in his eyes. Don’t compare her to your late sister. Is this it? Is this why Trash is participating?

While I was thinking about all that, the performance reached a natural break and moved on to the next scene. By the way, Filo had been singing in the background the whole time. Melty was playing the queen in her younger days. I think she did a pretty good job, all things considered.

It seems like they’re telling the story of Trash’s life in a humorous way, but there’s a problem with Keel’s acting as the lead. She goes into “dog mode” from time to time. Aside from that, combined with her androgynous appearance, she’d be captivating if she just acted seriously… Well, she’s not as much of a wooden actor as she was during Valentine’s Day, so I guess it’s fine.
Oh, Filo got competitive and transformed into her Filolial Queen form. Then the fans started chanting “Angel!” for Filo.
“Don’t let the curse win—become your true self!”
“A·n·g·e·l! A·n·g·e·l!”
“A·n·g·e·l! A·n·g·e·l!”
“A·n·g·e·l! A·n·g·e·l!”
“My Angel! Filo-chan!”
“My Angel!”
“Angel!”
“Filo-chan!”
“Go for it, Filo-chan!”

Ugh… Keel’s fans are totally turned off. At this rate, some people might start seeing Filo as the epitome of “creepy.” Hearing those fans’ words, Filo puffs out her cheeks in a pout and reverts to her human form.
“Why does Keel-kun get cheered on even when his form changes, but Filo doesn’t…?”

Give it up. Your true form is completely overlooked by the fans’ subconscious perception of you as a sexual object. In Keel’s case… he was treated like a pet to begin with, so everyone mentally pictures him in his dog form. Sure, there are probably some guys attracted to his androgynous looks, but since the audience is a different crowd, you can’t expect the kind of cheers you’re hoping for.
Eventually, the performance ended, the curtain came down, and the cast gathered on stage to take a bow. It was right after all that was over.
“Master—”
Filo waves at me as I watch from backstage.
“And now, I’d like to invite the Shield Hero, who is sponsoring this event!”
Melty steps forward dramatically, holding a microphone, and beckons me to come up. …I guess I have no choice. I walk onto the stage, stand before the huge crowd, and wave.
“Thanks, everyone, for coming today!”
Filo stood next to me, waving her hand.
“Today… I have a favor to ask of you all—”
“Huh? I didn’t hear anything about that…”
Filo was just rambling on on her own. Melty also tilted her head and met my gaze. Apparently, she had no idea what was going on either.
“Lately, Filo’s been so tired she’s completely wiped out—she needs a little break—”
Ugh! That Filo… what a hassle.
“It’s okay, right? Master?”
I want to say no. I want you to handle diplomatic relations with Melty as a goodwill gesture.
I glance silently at Melty, and she seems to agree with Filo. Well… even after the world finally achieved peace, she’s been working nonstop. Maybe I should let her take a vacation.
“If Melty’s okay with it… then I guess it’s fine?”
“That’s right. Filo-chan’s been working so hard, so I think she should take a little break. We’ve made pretty good progress on the diplomacy, too.”
In that case… fine. The fans are all looking at each other and nodding in agreement.
“True… Filo-tan’s health comes first, after all.”
“If she’s going to sing happily for us, a little rest is important! I can wait a hundred years if I have to.”
Yeah. If she puts her mind to it, Filo will surely live for over a hundred years, so it’ll be fine. Though I’m sure your lifespans will run out first.
“I agree!”
“I agree! Filo-chan, take a nice long rest—we’ll be waiting for the day we can see you again!”
I’m glad she has such understanding fans. Just as I was thinking that, Filo dropped a bombshell.
“You see, Filo—! I want to spend some time with my master, who I haven’t been able to see much lately!”

With that, Filo pressed her body against my arm and pulled me close. The way she looked… well, it reminded me of an idol introducing her new boyfriend to her fans. I had the illusion that Filo’s fans were staring at me with eyes filled with a cold yet passionate jealousy.
“Hahaha! Filo-tan’s such a little sweetheart. Getting along so well with Father like that…”

Of all the people here, Motoyasu is the only one who’s not quite right in the head, but at least he’s not jealous. I feel a pressure weighing down on me—the kind I can’t just brush off by saying, “It’s none of my business.” Filo’s fans start buzzing with excitement.
“Ah, Filo-tan, you’re so cute!　Me too! Me too!”

Keel, now in dog form, jumps on me and starts playing around. I get the feeling Keel’s fans are looking at me with envy… Either way, even I—who hardly ever gets nervous in situations like this… even I, the Shield Hero who saved the world—feel a chill running down my spine. Oh no. I have to say something… I feel like I’m about to get into trouble.

“Haha, as you can probably tell from the show, I’m like a surrogate parent to Filo. That’s why she’s being so affectionate, and Keel’s acting similarly—there’s nothing weird going on here, okay? Filo and Keel will always be your idols.”
I flashed a professional smile. The fans seemed to accept my explanation, at least for now.
“Um… Filo, you see—”
I covered Filo’s mouth to shut her up, as if to cover up something.
“So, after a short break, Filo will be resuming her activities—please look forward to it.”
“Uh—Filo—”
“You shut up!”
“Big bro! Big bro!”
“Yeah, yeah. Just be quiet for a second!”
“Naofumi-sama! Big Brother kept getting in the way, so I couldn’t meet you for a while, but I’ve finally made it!”
“Atla!”
Fohl grabbed Atla as she tried to approach me. Don’t make this any more complicated.
“Oh my, Big Brother? Aren’t you going to return Keel-kun’s feelings?”
“No—w-wait, that’s not—!”
Don’t make a scene in a place like this! Keeping an eye on the slightly suspicious looks from the crowd, I fled to the backstage area. Sigh… Seriously, those guys just cause nothing but trouble.
